# DUP001 arch-duplicate-code

A block of code copied three or more times.

## What it does

Fires once for a block of `dup_min_tokens` (default 50) or more tokens that occurs at `dup_min_occurrences` (default 3) or more places in the walk, across Rust, Python, TypeScript and C# files outside tests. Comments, whitespace and import statements are not tokens. A copy matches at one of three rungs: R1 the same tokens, R2 the same tokens with identifiers consistently renamed, R3 the same token shape with names and literals changed. A block reported at a stricter rung is not reported again at a looser one, and consecutive overlapping matches are merged into one block. The finding lists every site. Two copies are tolerated by default. `dup_min_tokens = 0` or `dup_min_occurrences` below 2 turns the rule off. A token match is exact, so the rule is never Unresolved.

## Why it matters

A block copied three times is one design maintained in three places; a fix to one copy silently misses the others.

## Remedy

Extract the shared block into a function or type that the sites call, or tune `[grimble] dup_min_tokens` and `dup_min_occurrences`.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```rust expect=fire file=src/lib.rs
pub fn first(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64) -> i64 {
    let sum = a + b * c - a;
    let diff = sum * b + c - a;
    let prod = diff * sum + b - c;
    let out = prod + diff * sum - a + b;
    out * 2 + sum - diff
}

pub fn second(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64) -> i64 {
    let sum = a + b * c - a;
    let diff = sum * b + c - a;
    let prod = diff * sum + b - c;
    let out = prod + diff * sum - a + b;
    out * 2 + sum - diff
}

pub fn third(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64) -> i64 {
    let sum = a + b * c - a;
    let diff = sum * b + c - a;
    let prod = diff * sum + b - c;
    let out = prod + diff * sum - a + b;
    out * 2 + sum - diff
}
```
